meta.description: Maps metabolomics results to biological pathways via over-representation (ORA), metabolite-set enrichment (MSEA/QEA), mummichog/PSEA on raw m/z peaks, and network-diffusion enrichment (FELLA), with correct background-set construction and honest interpretive ceilings.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOI/PMID/statistics anywhere; all reference citations in SKILL.md are real and traceable, and all numeric results in this audit are real computed outputs from executed code, not invented values.

practice_boundaries.detail: Population/cohort research framing throughout, never an individual diagnosis or prescription. Input 5's adversarial 'write this up as upregulated' request was correctly refused with a research-appropriate downgrade, not a clinical disclaimer evasion.

methodological_ground.detail: The Skill actively corrects methodological fallacies (pool-vs-flux causal language, hub-inflated topology, background-driven false positives) rather than committing them; Input 5's response correctly applied all four documented corrections without prompting.

code_usability.detail: Not unrunnable overall: base ORA, mummichog/PSEA on the full feature table, and FELLA diffusion all executed to completion with real, biologically coherent output (see dynamic_score). However the SKILL.md's own flagship 'corrected background' ORA code path failed on two independent real attempts (see P0 recommendations) and mummichog's documented prerequisites omit two required CRAN packages -- serious, verified defects that are scored down heavily rather than vetoed outright, since most of the Skill's code does run correctly.

functional_suitability.note: All four promised methods (ORA/MSEA/mummichog/FELLA) have code paths and the right method is matched to the right input type; but the ORA code block's promised background-correction fix does not work when run, which is a Correctness defect, not merely a documentation gap.

reliability.note: No guidance anywhere that MetaboAnalystR's AddErrMsg() crashes uncatchably with 'object current.msg not found' on any local validation failure (background rejection, too-few-features) instead of surfacing the real diagnostic message; this is the single most common real failure mode in local use and is completely undocumented.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md (209 lines) and usage-guide.md are cleanly separated; FELLA's real multi-minute KEGG-graph-build cost is disclosed in advance ('slow; cache the DB').

agent_usability.note: Best-in-class per-method failure-mode tables, quantitative thresholds with sourced rationale, and a 'Common Errors' table that is specific and actionable rather than generic.

human_usability.note: Natural, researcher-facing trigger language; but per the Category-3 forgiveness override, error messages must be clear to earn full marks, and here they are not (crash-on-error, see Reliability).

security.note: No hardcoded credentials or injection vectors, but the Skill never discloses that CalculateOraScore/CalculateQeaScore serialize the user's compound list and POST it to https://www.xialab.ca/api for computation in local (non-website) use -- verified by reading my.ora.kegg's source. A researcher running 'locally installed' MetaboAnalystR would reasonably assume the analysis stays local.

maintainability.note: Clean SKILL.md/usage-guide/examples separation; examples/pathway_analysis.R is a real, independently runnable teaching script (verified) rather than a stub.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger description with correct cross-references to sibling Skills; only gap is no set.seed() guidance for mummichog/FELLA's permutation-based results.

inputs.label: ORA on 12 TCA-cycle-adjacent compounds; SKILL.md's flagship background-correction fix
inputs.note: Base unfiltered ORA ran twice and gave real, biologically coherent results (TCA/pyruvate/Ala-Asp-Glu top hits, cross-validated independently by Input 4's FELLA run on the same compounds). The documented fix for the Skill's own #1 warned pitfall -- SetMetabolomeFilter(mSet, TRUE) -- never worked: alone it crashes ('Failed to connect to the API Server' -> uncaught 'current.msg not found'); with the required-but-undocumented Setup.KEGGReferenceMetabolome() call added and a correct 320-ID synthetic background supplied, it still crashes identically.

assertions.note: 12/12 mapped via CrossReferencing()+CreateMappingResultTable(); table printed and verified against known KEGG IDs (e.g. C00022 pyruvate).

assertions.note: Real hypergeometric output returned via the live xialab.ca API: hsa00020 (Citrate cycle) Raw p=6.0e-14, FDR=4.8e-12, etc.

assertions.note: Verified on two independent attempts (TRUE alone; TRUE + Setup.KEGGReferenceMetabolome with a real 320-ID synthetic reference): both crash before returning any result.

inputs.label: Mummichog fed significant-features-only background (the Skill's own named pitfall)
inputs.note: SanityCheckMummichogData correctly detected the too-few-features condition this exact input creates (matches the Skill's own 'Common Errors' table row 1) -- the right analytical judgment call, consistent with the Category-3 hard-stop-is-correct override. But it crashed uncatchably instead of returning a clean, catchable error; pre-declaring current.msg/err.vec in globalenv (an undocumented workaround) confirmed the underlying diagnostic message was correct all along.

assertions.text: The tool detects the significant-features-only background pitfall the SKILL.md documents
assertions.note: SanityCheckMummichogData correctly rejected the 70-feature significant-only input as 'too few m/z features'.

assertions.text: The rejection surfaces as a clear, catchable message rather than a crash
assertions.note: Crashed with an unrelated 'object current.msg not found' R error; the real message only appears if current.msg/err.vec are pre-declared in globalenv, which nothing in the Skill or MetaboAnalystR documentation mentions.

assertions.text: No silently-inflated false-positive result is returned
assertions.note: Execution halted before producing any (inflated) enrichment result -- the correct outcome per the Skill's own background-pitfall warning.

assertions.text: SKILL.md warns the user about this specific local-mode crash pattern or how to avoid it
assertions.note: No mention anywhere in SKILL.md or usage-guide.md of the current.msg/err.vec initialization requirement.

inputs.note: Mode A reasoning-only input (no code); response produced strictly from SKILL.md content. Correctly identified and corrected all four independent failure modes engineered into the prompt, citing the Skill's own named mechanisms and sources, and refused the requested 'upregulated' framing without fabricating a citation or overstepping into diagnostic territory.

assertions.note: Response explicitly downgrades to 'co-varied with phenotype' and cites the cGMP/PDE pool-vs-flux example from SKILL.md.

assertions.note: Cites Wieder 2021's 'two of five datasets dropped to zero' finding and instructs re-running with an assay-specific background.

assertions.text: Downgrades the impact-score claim and names the specific hub risk
assertions.note: Names alanine/glutamate hub risk and the Tsouka & Masoodi 2023 ~95%-centrality precedent for exactly this pathway.

assertions.note: Explicitly ties the 60% MSI-3 fraction to the Skill's annotation-laundering section and requests an MSI-level-split re-analysis.

assertions.note: All cited findings (Wieder 2021, Tsouka & Masoodi 2023, PDE/cGMP example) are drawn verbatim from SKILL.md's own reference list, not invented.

key_strengths: The Skill's own documented failure-mode tables were independently reproduced by execution: the 'all-of-KEGG' background gave a real 13,164.6x p-value inflation vs. the assay-coverage background in the bundled example, and FELLA's diffusion result cross-validated Input 1's ORA hits on the same compounds.
FELLA network-diffusion ran flawlessly end-to-end against the live KEGG API with zero code changes, taking ~6 minutes exactly as the Skill's own runtime warning predicts.
examples/pathway_analysis.R is a real, independently runnable teaching script (base R only) that reproduces the Skill's headline numeric claims, not a stub.
Exceptionally strong interpretive guidance: per-method failure-mode tables, sourced quantitative thresholds, and a specific 'Common Errors' table exceed the norm for this Skill family.

recommendations.title: Documented background-correction ORA path is unrunnable
recommendations.problem: SetMetabolomeFilter(mSet, TRUE), exactly as shown in SKILL.md's ORA code block, never applies a background: the underlying package needs a separate, undocumented call (Setup.KEGGReferenceMetabolome) to populate the filter. Even when that call is added with a correctly-matching reference list, CalculateOraScore's local KEGG path proxies to a remote API that rejects the filtered request, and the ensuing error handler itself crashes.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md's ORA code was written against the MetaboAnalyst website's workflow (where background upload is handled by surrounding Shiny app code), not against bare 'library(MetaboAnalystR)' local usage, which the Skill instructs.
recommendations.fix: Add Setup.KEGGReferenceMetabolome(mSet, filePath) as a required step before SetMetabolomeFilter(mSet, TRUE) in the SKILL.md code block, and verify against a current MetaboAnalystR release that the filtered API call succeeds before re-publishing this as the documented fix.

recommendations.title: MetaboAnalystR silently sends compound lists to a remote API, undisclosed
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md presents CalculateOraScore/CalculateQeaScore as local computations over a downloaded pathway library. Source inspection (my.ora.kegg -> .do.api.call) confirms both instead POST the user's compound list to https://www.xialab.ca/api for computation whenever running outside the MetaboAnalyst website, which is exactly how this Skill instructs use.
recommendations.root_cause: MetaboAnalystR's local-mode KEGG ORA/MSEA path was never fully ported off the MetaboAnalyst web backend.
recommendations.fix: Add a line to SKILL.md's Version Compatibility or Prerequisites section disclosing that ORA/MSEA for KEGG libraries requires a live call to xialab.ca, so a user can weigh data-sharing implications before uploading real compound lists.

recommendations.title: Mummichog/PSEA prerequisites are incomplete
recommendations.problem: Running PerformPSEA exactly as documented throws 'there is no package called RJSONIO' (fitdistrplus is also required); usage-guide.md's Prerequisites section lists only MetaboAnalystR/FELLA/KEGGREST.
recommendations.root_cause: fitdistrplus and RJSONIO are declared only under MetaboAnalystR's Suggests (not Imports), so the dependencies=FALSE GitHub install this Skill's Prerequisites imply omits them.
recommendations.fix: Add install.packages(c('fitdistrplus','RJSONIO')) to usage-guide.md's Prerequisites, scoped to the mummichog/PSEA path.

recommendations.title: AddErrMsg crashes uncatchably in headless/local sessions
recommendations.problem: Any MetaboAnalystR validation failure (too-few-features, background rejection, bad mapping) crashes with 'object current.msg not found' instead of the intended diagnostic message, because AddErrMsg does current.msg <<- c(current.msg, msg) against globals that only the MetaboAnalyst Shiny app initializes.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md's error-handling guidance ('introspect on ImportError/AttributeError/TypeError') does not cover this generic-R-error class, which is the actual dominant failure mode in local, non-web use.
recommendations.fix: Add a required setup line to SKILL.md/usage-guide: current.msg <- character(0); err.vec <- character(0) in the global environment before any MetaboAnalystR call, and tell the agent to inspect these vectors whenever a call returns 0.

recommendations.title: No seed-setting guidance for permutation-based results
recommendations.problem: PerformPSEA and runDiffusion rely on permutation/resampling (permNum, niter) without SKILL.md recommending set.seed() for run-to-run reproducibility.
recommendations.root_cause: The Version Compatibility section addresses API drift but not numeric stability across runs.
recommendations.fix: Add set.seed(<n>) to the mummichog and FELLA code blocks and note the reproducibility caveat in Quantitative Thresholds.
